name: Question 11
worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}) \\  & =y{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y{e}^{xy}) \\  & =y(y{e}^{xy}) \\  & ={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{xxy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xx}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xxy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{xx}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{xy}) \\  & =2y\cdot {e}^{xy}+{y}^{2}\cdot {e}^{xy}\cdot x \\  & =y(2+xy){e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Calculate fxxy(x,y) given that f(x,y)=exy.

a
(1+xy)exy
b
2(1+xy)exy
c
x(2−xy)exy
d
y(2+xy)exy
e
(2−xy)exy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the first-order derivative fx(x,y):

fx(x,y)=∂∂x(exy)=yexy

Next, we find fxx(x,y) by differentiating fx(x,y) with respect to x:

fxx(x,y)=∂∂x(fx(x,y))=∂∂x(yexy)=y(yexy)=y2exy

Finally, we find fxxy(x,y) by differentiating fxx(x,y) with respect to y:

fxxy(x,y)=∂∂y(fxx(x,y))=∂∂y(y2exy)=2y⋅exy+y2⋅exy⋅x=y(2+xy)exy
